```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8,
                      fig.height = 4.2, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(amorem)
source("case-helpers.R")
fmt <- function(x, d = 2) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ",")
pfmt <- function(p) if (p < 0.001) "< 0.001" else paste("=", fmt(p, 3))
```

# Time of day and day of week in company email

`radoslaw_email` records the internal email of a manufacturing company
(Michalski et al. 2011; Nurek & Michalski 2020, a company in Poland). Email is sent during working
hours and on working days, so the rate of every dyad depends on the clock. Time
of day and day of week are **global covariates**: at any instant they take the
same value for every sender–receiver pair. This case study estimates their
effect next to an endogenous reciprocity effect, using time-shifted
case-control sampling, and checks the fitted model with `gof_rem()`,
`gof_multivariate()` and `gof_auxiliary()`.

## Data and clock time

`time` counts days since the first email; `attr(radoslaw_email, "unix_origin")`
holds that instant as a Unix time. We use the first 30 days and convert each
time to Central European clock time.

```{r data}
data(radoslaw_email)
origin <- attr(radoslaw_email, "unix_origin")
ev <- radoslaw_email[radoslaw_email$time < 30 &
                     radoslaw_email$sender != radoslaw_email$receiver,
                     c("sender", "receiver", "time")]

clock <- function(t) as.POSIXlt(origin + t * 86400, origin = "1970-01-01",
                                tz = "Europe/Warsaw")
tod <- function(t) { p <- clock(t); p$hour + p$min / 60 + p$sec / 3600 }  # hours
dow <- function(t) { p <- clock(t); (p$wday + 6) %% 7 + tod(t) / 24 }     # 0 = Monday 00:00

c(events = nrow(ev), actors = length(unique(c(ev$sender, ev$receiver))),
  first = format(clock(min(ev$time))), last = format(clock(max(ev$time))))
```

```{r clock-figure, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 3.6, fig.alt = "Emails by hour of day and day of week, as a heatmap with totals per hour and per day"}
hr <- floor(tod(ev$time)); dy <- floor(dow(ev$time))
M <- table(factor(dy, levels = 0:6), factor(hr, levels = 0:23))
days <- c("Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun")
ramp <- grDevices::colorRampPalette(c("#FFFFFF", "#CFE6E6", pal[1], "#0B4F4F"))(64)
layout(matrix(c(2, 0, 1, 3), 2, byrow = TRUE), widths = c(5, 1), heights = c(1.1, 3))
par(mar = c(2.6, 3.2, 0.3, 0.3))
image(0:23, 0:6, t(log1p(M))[, 7:1], col = ramp, axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "", useRaster = TRUE)
axis(1, at = seq(0, 23, 3), labels = sprintf("%02d:00", seq(0, 23, 3)), tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.72,
     col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.6)
axis(2, at = 6:0, labels = days, las = 1, tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.72, col.axis = ink, line = -0.6)
par(mar = c(0.2, 3.2, 2.6, 0.3))
barplot(colSums(M), space = 0, border = NA, col = "#AEB5BA", axes = FALSE, names.arg = rep("", 24), xaxs = "i")
title_left("Emails by hour of day and day of week (Warsaw time)", "darker cell = more emails; bars: totals per hour and per day")
par(mar = c(2.6, 0.2, 0.3, 0.6))
barplot(rev(rowSums(M)), horiz = TRUE, space = 0, border = NA, col = "#AEB5BA", axes = FALSE, yaxs = "i",
        names.arg = rep("", 7))
```

```{r network-figure, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 5.6, fig.alt = "Email network of the 30 days among the actors of the busiest pairs, each actor's three strongest ties"}
pairs_n <- aggregate(list(w = rep(1, nrow(ev))), list(from = ev$sender, to = ev$receiver), sum)
und <- transform(pairs_n, a = pmin(from, to), b = pmax(from, to))
und <- aggregate(list(w = und$w), und[c("a", "b")], sum)
und <- und[order(-und$w), ]
ids <- head(unique(as.vector(rbind(und$a, und$b))), 60)
keep <- unique(unlist(lapply(ids, function(i) {
  r <- which((und$a == i | und$b == i) & und$a %in% ids & und$b %in% ids); head(r[order(-und$w[r])], 3) })))
bb <- und[keep, ]
lay <- withr::with_preserve_seed(layout_graph(data.frame(from = bb$a, to = bb$b, w = bb$w), ids = ids))
gc <- group_colours(lay$group)
act <- table(c(ev$sender, ev$receiver))
nodes <- data.frame(id = lay$id, x = lay$x, y = lay$y, size = as.numeric(act[lay$id]),
                    col = gc[as.character(lay$group)], label = NA)
ed <- pairs_n[paste(pairs_n$from, pairs_n$to) %in% c(paste(bb$a, bb$b), paste(bb$b, bb$a)), ]
same <- lay$group[match(ed$from, lay$id)] == lay$group[match(ed$to, lay$id)]
ed$col <- ifelse(same, gc[as.character(lay$group[match(ed$from, lay$id)])], "#B4BBC0")
g_of <- setNames(lay$group, lay$id)
among <- ev[ev$sender %in% lay$id & ev$receiver %in% lay$id, ]
within <- mean(g_of[among$sender] == g_of[among$receiver])
par(mar = c(1.8, 0.4, 2.8, 0.4))
draw_network(nodes, ed, directed = TRUE, max_lwd = 3)
title_left(sprintf("Who emails whom: %d employees of one company, %s emails in 30 days", length(act), fmt(nrow(ev), 0)),
           sprintf("the 60 employees of the busiest pairs, each one's three strongest ties; %s%% of their emails stay within a group",
                   fmt(100 * within, 0)))
mtext("dot size: emails sent and received  \u00b7  colour: group (modularity); grey lines join different groups",
      side = 1, line = 0.6, cex = 0.62, col = ink_soft)
```

```{r clock-numbers, include = FALSE}
h <- floor(tod(ev$time))
work <- mean(h >= 7 & h < 16)
wkend <- mean(floor(dow(ev$time)) >= 5)
```

`r fmt(100 * work, 1)`% of the emails are sent between 07:00 and 16:00, and
`r fmt(100 * wkend, 1)`% on Saturday or Sunday.

## Ordinary sampling cannot see a global covariate

With ordinary nested case-control sampling each control gets its event's time,
so a covariate that depends on time alone takes the same value for the event
and its control:

```{r no-shift}
cc0 <- sample_non_events(ev, seed = 1)
cc0$tod <- tod(cc0$time)
w0 <- widen_case_control(cc0, covariates = "tod")
summary(w0$d_tod)
```

Every event-minus-control difference is zero, so the time-of-day effect drops
out of the partial likelihood.

## Time-shifted sampling

`shift = "exponential"` draws one exponential shift per dyad and samples each
control from the dyads whose back-shifted time falls in the observation window
(here the 30 days of the slice). Each control is stored at its own time.

```{r shift}
cc <- sample_non_events(ev, seed = 1, shift = "exponential", window = c(0, 30))
sh <- attr(cc, "shift")
c(mean_shift_days = sh$mean, uninformative_events = length(sh$uninformative))
```

The endogenous covariate is reciprocity timing: the time since the receiver last
emailed the sender, mapped to a recency weight with `transform_recency()`
(1 when the receiver emailed the sender a moment ago, falling towards 0 as the
gap grows, and 0 when the receiver has not emailed the sender). On case-control data `endogenous_features()`
builds the history from the observed emails only, and each control is scored
at its own time. Time of day and day of week are read from each row's clock
time.

```{r covariates}
cc <- endogenous_features(cc, stats = "reciprocity_time_recent")
cc$recip <- transform_recency(cc$reciprocity_time_recent)
cc$recip[is.na(cc$recip)] <- 0
cc$tod <- tod(cc$time)
cc$dow <- dow(cc$time)
w <- widen_case_control(cc, covariates = c("recip", "tod", "dow", "time"))
summary(w$d_tod)
```

## Model

Time of day and day of week enter as cyclic smooths (`bs = "cc"`), the
residual trend over the 30 days as `nl(time)`, and reciprocity as a
time-varying effect `tv(recip)`. Because the controls carry their own times,
`tv(recip)` contributes \(\beta(t)\,x_{ev} - \beta(t^*)\,x_{nv}\), with \(t\)
the event time and \(t^*\) the control's time.

```{r fit}
fit <- rem(~ nl(tod, bs = "cc", k = 12) + nl(dow, bs = "cc", k = 8) +
             nl(time, k = 5) + tv(recip, k = 5),
           data = w, method = "gam", time = "time")
summary(fit)$s.table
```

```{r fit-figure, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 6.6, fig.alt = "Estimated smooth effects of time of day, day of week, the trend and time-varying reciprocity, with 95% bands"}
# draw_smooth() with chosen x-axis ticks
curve_panel <- function(d, col, ylab, at = NULL, labels = NULL, xlab = "") {
  lo <- d$fit - 1.96 * d$se; hi <- d$fit + 1.96 * d$se
  plot(d$x, d$fit, type = "n", ylim = range(lo, hi, 0), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
  abline(h = 0, col = rule, lwd = 1.2)
  if (is.null(at)) axis(1, tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.75, col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.5) else
    axis(1, at = at, labels = labels, tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.75, col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.5)
  axis(2, las = 1, tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.75, col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.5)
  mtext(xlab, side = 1, line = 2, cex = 0.75, col = ink_soft); mtext(ylab, side = 2, line = 2.3, cex = 0.75, col = ink_soft)
  polygon(c(d$x, rev(d$x)), c(lo, rev(hi)), col = alpha(col, 0.18), border = NA)
  lines(d$x, d$fit, col = col, lwd = 2.2)
}
op <- par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(3.4, 4, 3, 1))
curve_panel(smooth_data(fit$fit, 1), pal[1], "f(hour)", at = seq(0, 24, 4), labels = sprintf("%02d:00", seq(0, 24, 4)))
title_left("Time of day", "email log-rate relative to the daily mean; shaded: 95% interval")
curve_panel(smooth_data(fit$fit, 2), pal[2], "f(day)", at = 0:6 + 0.5,
            labels = c("Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"))
abline(v = 1:6, col = rule, lwd = 0.8)
title_left("Day of week", "labels mark the middle of each day; shaded: 95% interval")
curve_panel(smooth_data(fit$fit, 3), pal[3], "f(t)", xlab = "day of the slice")
title_left("Trend over the 30 days", "shaded: 95% interval")
curve_panel(smooth_data(fit$fit, 4), pal[5], expression(beta(t)), xlab = "day of the slice")
title_left("Reciprocity effect over time", "coefficient of the recency weight; shaded: 95% interval")
par(op)
```

```{r fit-numbers, include = FALSE}
st <- summary(fit)$s.table
curve_of <- function(j, grid, var, by) {
  sm <- fit$fit$smooth[[j]]
  nd <- data.frame(grid, 1); names(nd) <- c(var, by)
  as.vector(mgcv::PredictMat(sm, nd) %*% coef(fit$fit)[sm$first.para:sm$last.para])
}
hg <- seq(0, 24, length.out = 241)
f_tod <- curve_of(1, hg, ".X_tod", ".I")
dg <- seq(0, 7, length.out = 701)
f_dow <- curve_of(2, dg, ".X_dow", ".I")
tg <- seq(min(w$time_ev), max(w$time_ev), length.out = 200)
b_rec <- curve_of(4, tg, ".TP", ".XI_recip")
work_hours <- hg >= 8 & hg <= 16
```

In the `mgcv` summary the largest p-value of the four smooth terms is
`r formatC(max(st[, "p-value"]), format = "e", digits = 1)`. The time-of-day
curve is lowest at about `r fmt(hg[which.min(f_tod)], 1)` h and ranges from
`r fmt(min(f_tod[work_hours]))` to `r fmt(max(f_tod[work_hours]))` between
08:00 and 16:00. The day-of-week curve averages `r fmt(mean(f_dow[dg < 5]))`
from Monday to Friday and `r fmt(mean(f_dow[dg >= 5]))` on Saturday and Sunday
(log-rate scale, each curve centred by `mgcv`). Over the 30 days the
reciprocity coefficient \(\beta(t)\) ranges from `r fmt(min(b_rec))` to
`r fmt(max(b_rec))`. Shaded bands in the figure are 95% intervals.

## Goodness of fit of the fitted model

`gof_rem()` tests the fitted model directly. The functional-form test orders
the residuals by the covariate's value, and the time test cumulates the
residuals of a term over event time; both use a multiplier bootstrap that
accounts for the estimated coefficients.

```{r gof-rem}
g_tod  <- gof_rem(fit, "tod", test = "functional_form", n_sim = 1000, seed = 1)
g_dow  <- gof_rem(fit, "dow", test = "functional_form", n_sim = 1000, seed = 1)
g_time <- gof_rem(fit, "recip", test = "time", data = w, n_sim = 1000, seed = 1)
g_tod; g_dow; g_time
```

```{r gof-rem-figure, fig.height = 3.6, fig.alt = "Observed GoF processes against bootstrap processes"}
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 2.5, 1))
plot(g_tod, main = "time of day: functional form")
plot(g_dow, main = "day of week: functional form")
plot(g_time, main = "reciprocity: time")
par(op)
```

The functional-form test gives p `r pfmt(g_tod$p_value)` for time of day and
p `r pfmt(g_dow$p_value)` for day of week; the time test for the reciprocity
term gives p `r pfmt(g_time$p_value)`.

## Linear-model diagnostics on one week

`gof_multivariate()` and `gof_auxiliary()` take an event log and a linear
model, draw their own case-control sample and refit. Here they run on the first
week of the slice with count statistics: `gof_multivariate()` tests whether
`reciprocity_count` needs a smooth instead of a linear effect, and
`gof_auxiliary()` tests whether an unmodelled statistic carries signal the
model misses.

```{r gof-linear}
ev7 <- ev[ev$time < 7, ]
m <- c(reciprocity_count = "linear", transitivity_count = "linear")
gm <- gof_multivariate(ev7, m, covariate = "reciprocity_count", k_basis = 5,
                       n_sim = 1000, seed = 1)
ga <- gof_auxiliary(ev7, m, auxiliary = "sender_outdegree", n_sim = 1000,
                    seed = 1)
rbind(multivariate_reciprocity = c(statistic = gm$statistic, p_value = gm$p_value),
      auxiliary_sender_outdegree = c(statistic = ga$statistic, p_value = ga$p_value))
```

On the `r nrow(ev7)` emails of the first week, the multivariate test gives
p `r pfmt(gm$p_value)` for a non-linear reciprocity-count effect, and the
auxiliary test gives p `r pfmt(ga$p_value)` for the sender's out-degree.
